blocks.value: A variable of a class type doesn't store the object itself — it stores the object's memory address, called a reference. The actual object lives elsewhere in memory.

Because class-type variables hold references rather than the objects themselves, they're called reference types. This is why comparing two objects with == checks whether they're the exact same object in memory, not whether their contents match — use the equals() method to compare content instead, the same distinction covered for String comparisons earlier.
